features: Database seeding with reference legal data
long_desc:
AI4DRPM (Artificial Intelligence for Digital-Ready Policymaking) is a
Python microservice designed to facilitate the collection, annotation,
transformation, and compilation of legal documents and data.

It is part of the AI4DRPM project, which aims to enhance
digital-ready policymaking by leveraging artificial intelligence and
advanced data processing techniques.
name: AI4DRPM

desc_en: Domibus implements an eDelivery AS4 Access Point for interoperable, secure and reliable data exchange.
features: Secure and reliable message exchange – Implements the AS4 protocol for payload agnostic, encrypted, and signed messages with acknowledgements and retries, ensuring end-to-end confidentiality, integrity, and reliability.

Sample eDelivery AS4 Access Point – Conformant EC open-source implementation of the eDelivery AS4 profile that can be used to set up Access Points in distributed eDelivery secure exchange networks, ensuring interoperability between organisations.

Open-source, vendor-neutral, and extensible architecture – Maintained under the European Union Public Licence, with plugins/connectors (e.g., JMS, WS, File System) for integration with backend systems, allowing organisations to adapt and extend the code.

Management of participants and P-Modes – Handles metadata, communication parameters, and protocol configuration for multiple parties, including multi-tenancy support. Supports both static configuration and dynamic lookup using the BDXL/SMP standards.
Administration and monitoring tools – Web console and configuration tools for managing certificates, message filtering, monitoring, and logging.
Audit logging and traceability – Complete logging of message exchanges for compliance, dispute resolution, and auditing.
Compliance with EU legal standards – Aligned with ETSI standards defined for eIDAS (Q)ERDS and with EU security regulations for digital signatures, encryption, and secure exchange.
Web Services APIs (SOAP/REST) – Standard interfaces for sending, receiving, and managing messages, enabling integration with external systems.
long_desc: [Domibus](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/DIGITAL/pages/467110244/Domibus) is the sample software provided by the European Commission to implement an eDelivery AS4 Access Point for interoperable, secure and reliable data exchange. It is based on the [eDelivery AS4 profile](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/DIGITAL/pages/467117619/AS4+Access+Point+specifications), an open technical specification for the secure, web-based, payload-agnostic exchange of data or documents.
name: Domibus
short_desc: Domibus implements an eDelivery AS4 Access Point for interoperable, secure and reliable data exchange.

desc_en: DomiSML implements an eDelivery Service Metadata Locator for publishing the location of metadata necessary for message exchange.
features: Maintains a trusted registry of authorised Service Metadata Publishers (SMPs) and their registered network participants.
Ensures secure and reliable discovery of the location where participant service metadata is published, using a standards‑based lookup mechanism.
Adheres to EU eDelivery specifications, ensuring full interoperability across European digital systems.
Scales to support national or multi‑country ecosystems with millions of participants.
Provides clear administrative controls and comprehensive audit trails to support transparency, accountability, and good governance.
long_desc: [DomiSML](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/DIGITAL/pages/467118040/DomiSML) is the sample software provided by the European Commission to implement an eDelivery Service Metadata Locator for an eDelivery party  to discover the URLs of other counterparties using eDelivery Access Points and their corresponding metadata. It is based on  the [eDelivery BDXL profile](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/DIGITAL/pages/467118561/BDXL+specifications), an open technical specification for locating Access Points within a network, and on the [PEPPOL SML Specification](https://docs.peppol.eu/edelivery/), a technical specification defining a BDXL administration API.
name: DomiSML
short_desc: DomiSML implements an eDelivery Service Metadata Locator for publishing the location of metadata necessary for message exchange.

desc_en: DomiSMP implements an eDelivery Service Metadata Publisher for publishing and retrieving metadata necessary for message exchange.
features: Trusted participant registry and its service capabilities metadata (service descriptions) publication and retrieval.
Standards‑compliant metadata service aligned with EU eDelivery specifications to enable interoperability across EU systems.
Automatic endpoint discovery enabling seamless cross‑border and inter‑agency digital communication.
High availability and scalability to support large public‑sector networks.
Strong security and governance controls ensuring only verified organisations can register and exchange data.
User interface for managing participant registrations and service metadata, with support for bulk operations and API access.
Support for multiple document types, processes, and transport profiles to facilitate diverse message exchange scenarios.
Certificate and trust validation to ensure secure and trusted metadata publication and retrieval.
long_desc: [DomiSMP](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/DIGITAL/pages/467117783/DomiSMP) is the sample software provided by the European Commission to implement an eDelivery Service Metadata Publisher for publishing and retrieving data necessary for an eDelivery party to dynamically configure its system for message exchange with other parties using eDelivery. It is based on the [eDelivery SMP profile](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/DIGITAL/pages/467117984/SMP+specifications), an open technical specification for publishing service metadata within a 4-corner network.
name: DomiSMP
short_desc: DomiSMP implements an eDelivery Service Metadata Publisher for publishing and retrieving metadata necessary for message exchange.

desc_en: DSS is an open-source software library for electronic signature creation, augmentation and validation.
features: Electronic signatures (XAdES, CAdES, PAdES, JAdES and ASiC)
long_desc:
DSS (Digital Signature Services) is an open-source software library for electronic signature creation and validation.  DSS supports the creation and verification of interoperable and secure electronic signatures in line with European  legislation. In particular, DSS aims to follow the eIDAS Regulation and related standards closely. 
DSS can be re-used in an IT solution for electronic signatures to ensure that signatures are created and verified in line with European legislation and standards. DSS allows re-use in a variety of different ways: in an applet, in a standalone application or in a server application. DSS can also be used as a reference implementation for IT solutions which do not directly re-use it. Demos are also available to assist the use of DSS as a reference implementation.
The project is written in Java and issued under LGPL 2.1, a non-viral open source license.
name: DSS
short_desc: DSS is an open-source software library for electronic signature creation, augmentation and validation.

desc_en: DSS Demonstrations is the demonstration repository for project DSS.
name: DSS Demonstrations
short_desc: DSS Demonstrations is the demonstration repository for project DSS.

desc_en: DDC is Java library that implements a mechanism for Access Points to discover each other’s endpoints and capabilities without manual configuration.
features: Automatic participant lookup using SML to locate the SMP service where a network participant published its service capabilities metadata.
SMP metadata retrieval to obtain service metadata such as document types, transport profiles, and endpoint details.
Support for multiple transport profiles (e.g., AS4, AS2, etc.) to enable interoperability with different Access Points.
Support for multiple document types and processes to facilitate diverse message exchange scenarios.
Support for various party identifier schemes (e.g., eDelivery identifiers, PEPPOL identifiers) to accommodate different identification standards.
Certificate and trust validation to ensure secure and trusted metadata retrieval.
Compliance with eDelivery Dynamic Discovery specifications (SML/SMP standards, DNS-based addressing).
long_desc: [DDC](https://code.europa.eu/edelivery/dynamic-discovery-client/) is the sample Java library provided by the European Commission to implement an eDelivery dynamic discovery lookup for an eDelivery party to discover the URLs and metadata of other eDelivery Access Point counterparties. It is based on the [eDelivery BDXL specifications](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/DIGITAL/pages/467118561/BDXL+specifications), the [eDelivery SMP specifications](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/DIGITAL/pages/467117984/SMP+specifications) and the dynamic sender and receiver enhancements of the [eDelivery AS4 specifications](https://ec.europa.eu/digital-building-blocks/sites/spaces/DIGITAL/pages/467117619/AS4+Access+Point+specifications), an open technical specifications for locating Access Points within a network.
name: Dynamic Discovery Client (DDC)
short_desc: DDC is Java library that implements a mechanism for Access Points to discover each other’s endpoints and capabilities without manual configuration.

desc_en:
EUSurvey is the official online survey management tool of the European
Commission
long_desc:
EUSurvey is the official online survey management tool of the European
Commission. Its development was started in 2013 under the supervision of
[DIGIT](https://ec.europa.eu/dgs/informatics/index\_en.htm) and is
published as open source software under the terms of the EUPL public
license on GitHUB at [this
link](https://github.com/EUSurvey/EUSURVEY). 


EUSurvey is a servlet based application and can be installed on any system
that runs a JAVA servlet-container. The system’s development and reference
installation runs Apache Tomcat as the servlet container and uses a MySQL
database to store its information. The build process is assisted by Maven
for resolving external dependencies. This document describes the steps
that are necessary to compile and install the open source version of
EUSurvey. 


Please notice that EUSurvey can be configured to run on a large number of
different environments. 


[Here](https://github.com/EUSurvey/EUSURVEY)
you can find the README guide related to this software. The aim of such
document is to guide the interested user through the process of
installing a development environment and to deploy a working instance of
the EUSurvey system, with as less effor
name: EUSurvery
short_desc:
EUSurvey is the official online survey management tool of the European
Commission

desc_en: Web application for the online submission of KPI data for projects funded by European Union.
long_desc: Web tool to collect KPI from beneficiaries of EU funds. Customized for CBE Joint Undertaking, but open to customizable for other EU entities. The state of submissions is managed with a "Metroline" workflow similar to the one used in the COMPASS platform for EU grants management.
name: KPI Webtool
short_desc: Web application for the online submission of KPI data for projects funded by European Union.

long_desc:
LEOS (**L**egislation **E**diting **O**pen **S**oftware) is an open source

software designed to help those involved in draﬅing legislation, which in

itself is a complex knowledge-intensive process, by supporting eﬃcient

online collaboration. Comments, suggestions, version control, co-edition,

everything is there. Regarding the structure, that is where we aim to be

as restrictive as possible and this is not because we are conservative,

but because this helps the draﬅers follow the rules and avoid mistakes.

Content is stored in an XML format, currently Akoma Ntoso V3.

desc_en:
Simulation tool that developed by the European Commission used for
determining CO2 emissions from Heavy Duty Vehicles.
long_desc:
VECTO is the simulation tool that has been developed by the European
Commission and is used for determining CO2 emissions and Fuel Consumption
from Heavy Duty Vehicles (trucks, buses and coaches) with a Gross Vehicle
Weight above 3500kg.

Since 1 January 2019, the tool is mandatory for new trucks under certain
vehicle categories in application to the certification legislation under
type approval. 

CO2 emissions and fuel consumption data determined with VECTO, together
with other related parameters, must be monitored and reported to the
Commission by Member States and manufacturers, and made publicly available
for each of those new trucks.

Five different mission profiles for trucks and five different mission
profiles for buses and coaches have been developed and implemented in the
tool to better reflect the current European fleet. VECTO is a downloadable
executable file designed to operate on a single computer.

The inputs for VECTO are characteristic parameters to determine the power
consumption of every relevant vehicle component. Among others, the
parameters for rolling resistance, air drag, masses and inertias, gearbox
friction, auxiliary power and engine performance are input
name: vecto-sim
short_desc:
Simulation tool that developed by the European Commission used for
determining CO2 emissions from Heavy Duty Vehicles.
